decisions.reason: While floor-level shower drainage is close to our core knowledge, its absence as a distinct offering through 2020-2021 suggests the line has likely been absorbed into newer integrated systems, so we would withdraw the standalone product.

As a design-led shower drainage flagship, it remains strongly aligned with our accumulated drainage, design, and installation know-how, giving us a good basis to refine and continue it despite the need for portfolio updates.
The integrated-slope shower element fits our expertise in installation reliability, waterproofing, and renovation-friendly solutions, so we are more likely to keep improving it than to exit it.

Although technically related to drainage, the backflow-protected basement drain sits further from our main bathroom and shower focus, and with limited visible continuation it is more efficient to reallocate resources elsewhere.
The air-admittance valve is the most peripheral to our core absorptive base in shower and floor drainage systems, so weak strategic fit makes withdrawal the most likely choice.
